candidates.summary: - Kala-azar is emerging in Uttarakhand, including among residents with no travel history to endemic areas, challenging the assumption that the vector-borne disease is confined to hot, humid lowlands. - Gaps in disease surveillance mean cases diagnosed at hospitals outside Uttarakhand are missing from state records, obscuring the extent of local transmission. - Changing environmental conditions, livestock as potential sandfly hosts and the spread of sandflies to higher elevations raise questions about how the disease is transmitted beyond endemic regions. - Although India has made significant progress towards elimination, gaps in surveillance and vector control could undermine these gains, particularly in states not covered by dedicated elimination programmes.
